manifest.name: Payment Provider: Stripe
manifest.summary: An Irish-American payment provider covering the US and many others.

relations: no new fields; 14 methods overriding payment's request/notification hooks

models._description: Payment Token (saved Stripe card / SCA migration)

security.note: No own ACL/rules; relies on payment's security and on base.group_system field groups guarding stripe_secret_key / stripe_webhook_secret.

views.note: No own model views; xml_loc=134 is view inheritance (payment.provider form: Stripe keys + 'Generate Webhook' / 'Verify Apple Pay domain' buttons), QWeb templates (payment_stripe_templates.xml inline form, payment_templates.xml loads the Stripe.js SDK script tag only on pages with a payment form), plus payment_provider_data.xml.

behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._stripe_create_intent / _send_payment_request -> outbound POST to api.stripe.com (PaymentIntent / SetupIntent)
behavioral_notes.observation: The outbound acquirer call (gap #7) is centralized through payment's payment.provider._send_api_request, which payment_stripe targets at https://api.stripe.com/v1/ via _build_request_url and authenticates with 'AUTHORIZATION: Bearer <stripe_secret_key>' + 'Stripe-Version: 2019-05-16' headers (_build_request_headers, secret fetched sudo via utils.get_secret_key). _stripe_create_intent POSTs to 'setup_intents' for a validation operation, else to 'payment_intents' (amount in minor units, capture_method manual/automatic from provider.capture_manually, payment_method_types[] mapped via const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING, expand[]=payment_method), passing an idempotency_key for payment intents and offline=True for off-session token charges. _send_payment_request (token/offline charge) and _get_specific_processing_values (online_direct inline flow) both create the intent and hand the client_secret to the front-end Stripe.js Elements. None of this server-to-server HTTP is visible in Python field/model metadata. NB: per README the legacy Checkout-Session redirect flow was replaced by the deferred Payment Intents API in v16.4 (this module creates PaymentIntents, not Checkout Sessions).

behavioral_notes.element: StripeController.stripe_webhook (/payment/stripe/webhook) -> Stripe-Signature (webhook secret) verification + tx state update
behavioral_notes.observation: The public, csrf=False POST webhook at /payment/stripe/webhook parses the Stripe event, and for events in const.HANDLED_WEBHOOK_EVENTS (payment_intent.{processing,amount_capturable_updated,succeeded,payment_failed,canceled}, setup_intent.succeeded, charge.refunded, charge.refund.updated) locates the tx via payment.transaction._search_by_reference (by the intent's 'description' = Odoo reference, or by provider_reference for refund updates) and then calls _verify_signature BEFORE acting. _verify_signature implements Stripe's manual scheme (https://stripe.com/docs/webhooks/signatures): it reads the 'Stripe-Signature' header, rejects events older than WEBHOOK_AGE_TOLERANCE (10 min) or with a missing v1 signature with werkzeug Forbidden, then HMAC-SHA256s '<timestamp>.<raw-body>' with stripe_webhook_secret and compares with hmac.compare_digest (constant-time). On success it enriches the event (for setup_intents / tokenized payment_intents it fetches the PaymentMethod via GET payment_methods/<id>; for charge.refunded it paginates GET refunds and creates child refund transactions) and calls tx_sudo._process('stripe', data), driving payment's guarded state machine (_set_pending/_set_authorized/_set_done/_set_canceled/_set_error). The redirect-return route /payment/stripe/return instead GETs the PaymentIntent/SetupIntent from Stripe to confirm state, then _process + redirect to /payment/status. Signature trust, the constant-time compare, and the inbound state transition are all invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: Stripe Connect onboarding via odoo proxy (action_start_onboarding / _stripe_create_account_link / OnboardingController)
behavioral_notes.observation: action_start_onboarding (override of payment) gates on const.SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES (RedirectWarning if the company country is unsupported), then _stripe_fetch_or_create_connected_account and _stripe_create_account_link POST 'accounts' / 'account_links' through Odoo's Stripe proxy at https://stripe.api.odoo.com/api/stripe/ (const.PROXY_URL, is_proxy_request=True, payload wrapped by _prepare_json_rpc_payload with proxy_data). The returned Stripe-hosted account_onboarding URL becomes an ir.actions.act_url redirect; Stripe sends the merchant back to /payment/stripe/onboarding/return (auth=user -> redirects to the provider form action) or /payment/stripe/onboarding/refresh (auth=user -> mints a fresh account link when the previous expired). Two @api.constrains forbid setting a connected-account provider to 'test' and forbid 'enabled' while onboarding is ongoing (_stripe_has_connected_account/_stripe_onboarding_is_ongoing are hooks returning False in core, fully implemented by a Stripe-Connect-Platform override). action_stripe_create_webhook auto-registers the webhook (POST webhook_endpoints with const.HANDLED_WEBHOOK_EVENTS) and stores the returned signing secret; action_stripe_verify_apple_pay_domain registers the web domain (POST apple_pay/domains) and serves the association file at /.well-known/...

When tx.tokenize is set, payment's engine calls _tokenize after a successful authorized/done intent; payment_stripe._extract_token_values mines the Stripe objects to vault a payment.token: provider_ref = the Stripe Customer id (POSTed up-front by _stripe_create_customer with the partner's billing details), stripe_payment_method = the PaymentMethod id, payment_details = card last4, and stripe_mandate when an eMandate was set up (Indian recurring flow, _stripe_prepare_mandate_options, currencies in const.INDIAN_MANDATES_SUPPORTED_CURRENCIES). Subsequent off-session charges (operation online_token/offline) POST a PaymentIntent with confirm=True, off_session=True, customer=token.provider_ref, payment_method=token.stripe_payment_method, mandate=token.stripe_mandate. Pre-SCA tokens are lazily migrated by payment.token._stripe_sca_migrate_customer (GET payment_methods for the customer, store the id). _send_refund_request (POST refunds), _send_capture_request (POST payment_intents/<id>/capture) and _send_void_request (POST payment_intents/<id>/cancel) round out the authorize/capture/void/refund operations, each re-using _process to fold the response into the state machine.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, keys, SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; two outbound endpoints -- https://api.stripe.com/v1/ (direct REST, Bearer secret-key auth) and https://stripe.api.odoo.com/api/stripe/ (Odoo's Stripe Connect proxy, jsonrpc) -- declared in const.py and models/payment_provider.py. No 'requests' import here: HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine, which payment_stripe configures via the _build_request_url / _build_request_headers / _parse_response_* hook overrides. On the browser side the Stripe.js v3 Web Elements SDK is loaded by a <script> tag (payment_templates.xml) on pages showing the payment form -- a second, client-side channel to Stripe. This dual server-to-server + client-side acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of it is reachable from model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (static) -- Stripe.js inline form + Express Checkout patches
behavioral_notes.observation: 3 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds (gap #3). The module patches two shared payment widgets rather than registering new components: PaymentForm.prototype (static/src/interactions/payment_form.js) drives the Stripe.js Payment Element -- it consumes the inline-form values JSON from payment.provider._stripe_get_inline_form_values (publishable_key, minor_amount, currency, capture_method, billing_details, payment method mapping) to mount Elements and confirm the intent client-side using the client_secret -- and ExpressCheckout.prototype (static/src/interactions/express_checkout.js, with stripe_options.js) implements the express-checkout (Apple Pay / Google Pay payment-request button). Assets load into web.assets_frontend (manifest globs static/src/**/*). These browser interactions and the Stripe.js SDK are invisible to Python metadata (gap #3).

external_integrations.sdk: Stripe.js v3 (browser Web Elements); server side uses no python SDK -- HTTP via payment.provider._send_api_request
external_integrations.auth: Bearer <stripe_secret_key> + Stripe-Version header (direct API); Odoo jsonrpc proxy (Connect)
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration. Outbound server-to-server REST to api.stripe.com (PaymentIntent / SetupIntent / Customer / Refund / capture / cancel / webhook_endpoints / apple_pay) authenticated with a secret API key; Stripe Connect onboarding routed through Odoo's stripe.api.odoo.com proxy; a parallel client-side Stripe.js Elements channel; and inbound settlement via a Stripe-Signature-verified webhook plus a redirect-return route. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Stripe endpoints, the Bearer-key auth, the webhook HMAC trust, or the browser SDK channel are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading const.py + the model/controller code.

Onboard-Merchant: action_start_onboarding -> Stripe Connect account + account_link via odoo proxy -> Stripe-hosted onboarding -> /payment/stripe/onboarding/return -> provider enabled

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_stripe is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the cardholder/payer and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Stripe's card network. It exhibits the three mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (Stripe Connect onboarding, webhook registration, key management, Apple Pay domain verification), service provisioning (creating the PaymentIntent/SetupIntent and confirming the charge per transaction), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server api.stripe.com link, the Stripe.js client channel, and the signed-webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Stripe realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the parent payment.metamodel.json (network/support) and contrasts with account_payment (support/support), whose own logic is ledger record-keeping rather than mediation.

standard_capabilities: direct card payment via Stripe PaymentIntents with client-side Stripe.js Elements (SCA/3DS handled by Stripe)
tokenization / saved cards (Stripe Customer + PaymentMethod), including off-session recurring and Indian eMandates
full manual capture, void, and full + partial refunds
express checkout (Apple Pay / Google Pay) via the payment-request button
asynchronous settlement via a Stripe-Signature-verified webhook plus a redirect-return confirmation route
Stripe Connect quick self-onboarding and one-click webhook creation
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting card payments through Stripe in a supported country
save-card-for-later and tokenized recurring/subscription charges (off_session PaymentIntents)
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
merchant self-onboarding to Stripe via Connect rather than manual API-key entry
multi-currency acceptance (minor-unit + zero/3-decimal special-case handling in const.CURRENCY_DECIMALS)
common_gaps: partial MANUAL capture is explicitly NOT implemented (support_manual_capture='full_only'; README 'Not implemented')
full Stripe Connect platform behavior (managing connected sub-accounts, _stripe_has_connected_account / _stripe_onboarding_is_ongoing real logic) is left as hooks for a separate module
the public-URL requirement for webhooks means local/dev instances need a tunnel; without a webhook secret signature verification is skipped (events ignored with a warning)
API version pinned to 2019-05-16 in const.py -- newer Stripe features / payment methods need code changes
country support is bounded by const.SUPPORTED_COUNTRIES; unsupported regions cannot onboard via Connect
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here

Which downstream modules consume the settled Stripe transactions (account_payment, sale, subscription) and how partial captures/voids split across child transactions.
Whether instances actually register the webhook (stripe_webhook_secret set) vs rely solely on the redirect-return route, since signature checks are skipped when the secret is empty.
